question: Should OpenClaw adopt a core-owned skill permission manifest contract now, and should the first phase be audit-only metadata, install-time consent, or enforced capability gating?
rationale: The choice defines a public security boundary across skills, ClawHub, plugin hooks, install/update UX, signing roots, trust scoring, and runtime enforcement, so automation should not pick the permanent contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt staged advisory manifest
options.body: Define a small versioned permission vocabulary first, surface it in install/status/audit policy paths, and track consent, signing, attestation, and enforcement as explicit follow-ups.

options.title: Design enforcement before schema
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers settle default-deny runtime enforcement, approval UX, update diffs, and migration behavior together.

options.title: Keep it external for now
options.body: Treat external packages and ClawHub scan pages as the primary permission surface unless a missing OpenClaw core/API seam is proven.

recommendation.title: Adopt staged advisory manifest
recommendation.body: Define a small versioned permission vocabulary first, surface it in install/status/audit policy paths, and track consent, signing, attestation, and enforcement as explicit follow-ups.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the clearest product/security decision signal in this issue and have current provenance across the central skills and docs surfaces.
